what_worked: Pareto curve with median-vs-mean distinction is a genuinely useful framing of revenue skew.
fix_next: Top-10 share is 49.6%, not top-1%; category mean MRR figures appear fabricated—verify every number against the actual dataset.
verdict: Polished consulting template with several material factual errors undermining credibility.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1: '49.6% captured by Top 1%' — the 49.6% figure is the Top-10 share, not Top-1%. Slide 2: 'Top 10% control 83.7%' — unverifiable and likely inflated. Slide 3: 'Top Categories: E-commerce ($20.8k), Analytics ($18.8k), Education ($17.5k)' — these mean MRR figures are wildly inconsistent with reference data (E-comm total is $1.1M across 19 companies ≈ $58.5k mean revenue, not MRR; Analytics $368k/19 ≈ $19.4k total revenue, not MRR). The deck conflates 30-day revenue with MRR throughout without justification. Slide 3: B2B mean $13,150 vs B2C $5,102 — reference shows B2B/B2C median multiples of ~2.35x/2.30x and means of ~7.97x/8.44x; the presented figures don't align. Slide 1: '500K+ Active Subscriptions' — unverifiable hero metric presented without sourcing. Slide 4: '82.2% missing visitor data' — not verifiable from reference but plausible; minor concern.

evidence.insight: Slide 2 usefully distinguishes median ($282) from mean ($13.5k) and highlights concentration risk. Slide 3 correlation matrix adds analytical depth. However, the 'Top Categories' ranking by mean MRR appears fabricated, undermining the insight's foundation.
evidence.narrative: Five slides follow a logical arc: summary → distribution → drivers → risks → recommendations. The thesis (B2B subscription depth > volume) is stated clearly and revisited. However, the narrative is generic consulting-speak ('elite performance,' 'strategic blind spots') rather than data-driven storytelling.
evidence.framing: Audience is implied (ecosystem leadership/investors) but never explicitly stated. No definitions of MRR vs 30-day revenue. No mention of 274 missing category values or 288 missing audience_type values, which directly affect the B2B/B2C and category analyses. No limitations section.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple material errors: the 49.6% top-10 share is attributed to top-1%; category mean MRR figures don't match reference totals/counts; the deck uses 'MRR' and '30-day revenue' interchangeably without noting they are the same field; B2B/B2C figures are not consistent with reference multiples; 'Top 10% = 83.7%' is unverified.
evidence.visual: Clean, consistent design system with teal/dark navy palette. Pareto curve is well-executed with appropriate annotations. Correlation heatmap is readable. Scatter plot on slide 4 uses log scale appropriately. Layout is professional. However, visual sameness across slides suggests template-driven production.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy consulting language throughout: 'elite performance,' 'strategic blind spots,' 'subscription-driven moats,' 'roadmap for elite performance.' The 'LEADERSHIP ACTION' boxes on every slide are formulaic. Recommendations are generic enough to apply to any SaaS dataset.
